newsitem.title: USA: Eastman less cyclical than most chemicals.
newsitem.headline: Eastman less cyclical than most chemicals.

text.p: Eastman Chemical Co is less cyclical than other chemical companies, chief executive Earnest W. Deavenport Jr. said Tuesday.

He told the Nashville Society of Financial Analysts operating earnings data indicate Eastman is less cyclical than many of its peer companies, pointing out that more than half of Eastman's sales are from industries that are not typically cyclical.
He also noted Eastman's wide product diversity, with chemicals and fibers accounting for 58 percent of sales revenue and plastics at 42 percent.

"Eastman is the world leader in polyester plastics for packaging," Deavenport said. "We're a major supplier of cellulose acetate tow," the long fiber used in cigarette filters, "and a leader in coatings, fine chemicals and many specialty chemicals and plastics markets.

"Our products are the lifeblood of everyday living. In fact, during a normal day, it would be almost impossible not to come in contact with something that has an Eastman product in it," he told the analysts.
Deavenport said Eastman's mission is "to create superior value through our strategy of aggressive global growth."

One goal is to increase sales outside the United States to 50 percent; Eastman reached 38 percent during first half 1996. Net assets outside the United States were at 13 percent through the first half, with a company goal of 30 percent.
"At Eastman, we have worked hard to align employee compensation and shareowners' interests," Deavenport said. "The way we've chosen to do this is to create shareowners within our company."

Eastman employees have five percent of their annual pay at risk, with the opportunity to earn up to 30 percent of their annual pay as a bonus depending on the company's financial performance, he said.
Eastman directs five percent of employees' pay into an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, and managers participate in various other annual performance plans.
"Employees can quickly get to the place where a significant amount of their compensation and personal wealth is tied to Eastman stock," Deavenport said.
"We believe this is good. We see evidence of people making decisions about the company based on what's in the best interest of shareowners like themselves."
